svg.text: 1982 RX-7 FB · electrical architecture
One picture of the whole system · red = heavy feed · black = harness leg · dotted box = wired and capped
REAR — cargo bin, tank, rear lamps, sill
Ionic S9 lithium · master disconnect · Class-T 150 A
MRBF 200 A on the post for the starter run
Rear ground stud: battery 2 AWG negative + the L4 star
NOCO BG27 box, clamped in every axis
L4 REAR leg
defog · fuel pump · amplifier
tail · brake · turn · reverse
interior lamp · fuel sender
door jamb ladder · luggage lamp
rear star ground
SILL NODE
D1 / D2 door receptacles
ground stud to chassis
K5–K8 sockets, empty
F8 / F9 / F14 holders, empty
every door conductor capped
GROUND RULE
One star node per zone, straight to bare chassis.
No ground crosses a leg connector.
The fuel pump has its own return.
The engine block is strapped to the body for cranking.
DASH — the removable plate and the five drops
ECUMaster PMU-24 DL
39-way SICMA · 150 A stud
10 × 25 A · 6 × 15 A · 8 × 7 A outputs
A1–A8 + A15 / A16 ladder inputs
CAN1 laptop · CAN2 vehicle
every output is a software fuse
Plate hardware
always-hot busbar · ground bus
fuse blocks A–D, one source each
F12 F15 F16 sealed inlines
K1 K2 K11 K12 + 6 spare sockets
wake strip · 2 sense stages · bias
DASH POST — 15 leg receptacles + 5 drops + 2 lugs
DP-CLU factory cluster · DP-DIAG laptop port · DP-ICU / DP-DCU / DP-KEY wired and capped
every splice lives here, inside the box — never in a leg
L3 DASH leg
ignition + light switch ladders · turn · wiper · hazard · brake · horn · wink
blower · head unit · USB-C · illumination · glove box · parking brake
dash star ground = the plate ground bus
The 2 AWG feed from the Class-T lands on the busbar. The starter cable never comes here.
The factory cluster stays: DP-CLU feeds its gauges, lamps and indicators from day one.
ENGINE BAY — firewall grommet boundary
L1 ENGINE leg
coils O12 · start relay K9 (O21) · excitation F15
water temp · oil pressure · tach · fluid level
inhibitor P/N + R contacts
LS reserves capped · every unused cavity plugged
K9 + F17 + F18 at the starter B+ stud
block star ground + 2 AWG strap to chassis
FRONT — nose, cowl, buckets
L2 FRONT leg
headlights O2 / O3 · pop-ups K1 / K2 off O1
wipers O8 / O9 · washer K12 · horns O11
turn O17 / O18 · park + markers O6
pop-up transit + wiper park ladders
front star ground on the radiator support
2 AWG through the tunnel, pull string beside it
HOW TO READ THE SYSTEM
Power: battery → disconnect → Class-T → 2 AWG → busbar → PMU stud. The starter is its own run off the post.
Four legs leave the dash post, cut by what comes out of the car as one piece (engine · nose · dash · rear).
Every switch is a resistor ladder to ground on one wire; no switch carries load current.
The PMU switches every load and protects every wire with a software fuse. Plate relays exist only where a
channel is shared (pop-ups, washer) or a 30 A audio feed must live outside the PMU (K11).
Everything the car may gain later has its wire run now, terminated and capped.
STATUS WORDS
LIVE — wired, connected, enabled at migration.
CAPPED — wire cut, terminated in its cavity, far end sealed and labelled CAPPED. Nothing on it.
PLUG — engine-leg cavity with a sealing plug and no wire (the bay carries no stubs).
EMPTY — relay socket or fuse holder fitted and labelled with nothing in it.
Counts: 15 leg + 2 door + 5 drop housings + 2 lugs + the PMU connector = 25 mated pairs · 39 PMU cavities, all allocated
